raw_case_text:
A 38-year-old male patient, diagnosed with retroviral infection and disseminated tuberculosis presented with weakness and numbness of the right hand of 2 weeks duration. He also noticed an edematous reddish raised lesion on the inner aspect of right hand, which he attributed to the topical agent he used for relieving the numbness. Pain was present on the right elbow and forearm. The patient had been on antitubercular therapy (ATT) followed by antiretroviral therapy (ART), 5 months prior to presentation at our department. The CD4 count was 67 cells/muL during initiation of HAART.
Dermatological examination showed a single well-defined erythematous plaque, 20 x 5 cm with raised borders on the ulnar aspect of right hand and distal forearm, extending to the palm [Figures 1 and 2]. A satellite lesion was present on the upper part of forearm, which also showed erythema and edema. All modalities of sensations were lost in these lesions. Both ulnar nerves were thickened with tenderness on the right side. Slit skin smears from the earlobe, lesional, and normal skin were negative. Histopathological examination showed dermal edema, diffuse granulomas composed of Langhans type giant cells, surrounded by epithelioid cells, lymphocytes, multinucleated giant cells, and fibroblasts with perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate, consistent with Hansen's disease borderline tuberculoid type, with features suggesting type 1 lepra reaction [Figures 3-6]. AFB stain was negative. CD4 count after 5 months showed a rise to 160 cells/muL. The viral RNA load was not measured due to lack of facilities.
Thus correlating the clinical, bacteriological, and histopathological features, a diagnosis of Hansen's disease borderline tuberculoid with type 1 lepra reaction presenting as IRIS was made. MB-MDT was started, avoiding rifampicin from the regimen, as patient was also on ATT. HAART was continued and systemic steroids were also given in tapering doses. On follow up there was marked alleviation of his symptoms. However, the patient succumbed within 3 months to a brain tuberculoma.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old male with HIV and disseminated tuberculosis presented 5 months after starting anti-tubercular and antiretroviral therapy with a 2-week history of right hand weakness and numbness, right elbow and forearm pain, and an edematous erythematous plaque on his right hand.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Five months after initiating anti-tubercular therapy (ATT) followed by highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART), the patient developed a 2-week history of right hand weakness and numbness, right elbow and forearm pain, and a raised erythematous edematous plaque over the ulnar aspect of his right hand and distal forearm (which he initially attributed to a topical ointment applied for numbness).
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection (baseline CD4 count 67 cells/uL at HAART initiation) and disseminated tuberculosis on ATT for 5 months.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right hand weakness and anesthesia, right elbow/forearm neuralgic pain, and edematous erythematous skin plaques.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatological examination revealed a well-defined 20 x 5 cm erythematous, edematous plaque with raised borders over the ulnar aspect of the right hand and distal forearm extending onto the palm, accompanied by an erythematous, edematous satellite lesion on the proximal right forearm. Neurological examination demonstrated complete loss of all sensory modalities (touch, pain, and temperature) over the cutaneous lesions and bilateral ulnar nerve thickening with tenderness on the right.
objective.routine_investigations: CD4 T-cell count at 5 months of HAART had increased from 67 cells/uL to 160 cells/uL (HIV viral load was unavailable).
objective.advanced_workup: Slit-skin smears from the earlobe, lesional skin, and normal skin were negative for acid-fast bacilli (AFB). Lesional skin biopsy was performed for H&E and AFB staining.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Skin biopsy revealed dermal edema, diffuse tuberculoid granulomas composed of Langhans and multinucleated giant cells, epithelioid cells, lymphocytes, and fibroblasts with perivascular lymphocytic infiltration and negative AFB staining, confirming borderline tuberculoid (BT) Hansen's disease with a Type 1 reversal reaction presenting as unmasking immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). He was treated with rifampicin-sparing multibacillary multidrug therapy (since rifampicin was already included in his ongoing ATT), continued HAART, and tapering systemic corticosteroids with marked neurological and cutaneous improvement, but died 3 months later due to a cerebral tuberculoma.
